paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD is worth praising, and this psalm gives you reasons instead of just a command. He is good (Psalm 135:3). He has chosen Israel as "His treasured possession" (Psalm 135:4). He is "above all gods" (Psalm 135:5). Praise in this psalm isn't a mood you have to work up, it's an answer to who He is.

Now look at what the psalm does with the idols. They're "silver and gold, made by the hands of men," with mouths that can't speak and ears that can't hear (Psalm 135:15-17). Then comes the line that stops me cold: "Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them" (Psalm 135:18). Whatever you put your trust in shapes you. Trust something that can't hear or help, and you end up empty too. Trust the LORD, who does all that pleases Him (Psalm 135:6), and you're held by Someone who is alive.

That's why the psalm opens and closes with "Hallelujah!" (Psalm 135:1, 21). It calls everybody in, from the house of Israel to "you who fear the LORD" (Psalm 135:19-20). So, baker, what are you leaning on today? Lean on the One whose name "endures forever" (Psalm 135:13), and let your praise be the loud, happy answer. I'll be right here in my apron, hollering along with you.
